The dried fruit of Semecarpus anacardium (Anacardium orien- tale). It contains a minimum 6.0% of total phenol derivatives ex- pressed as eugenol. Profile Various parts of the oriental cashew, Semecarpus anacardium (Anacardiaceae), and their preparations are used in traditional In- dian medicine. The oil contains bhilawanols, irritant substances reputed to have cytotoxic action. Homoeopathy. The dried ripe fruit of oriental cashew is used in homoeopathic medicines under the following names: Anacar- dium; Semecarpus anacardium; Anacardium orientale; Anac. or. Pharmacopoeias. In Chin., Eur. (see p.vii), and Jpn. Chin. and Jpn also include cassia bark which may be known as cinnamon bark. In some countries cassia oil is known as cinna- mon oil (p.2283). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Cassia Oil). The oil obtained by steam distillation of the leaves and young branches of Cinnamomum cassia (C. ar- omaticum). It contains 70 to 90% of cinnamaldehyde. A clear, mobile, yellow to reddish-brown liquid, with a characteristic odour of cinnamaldehyde. Store in well-filled airtight containers. Protect from light and heat.
